cards.example: Courtesy is a habit, not a mood.

cards.definition: making someone feel welcome in your space
cards.example: Hospitality is why people come back.

cards.definition: standing with someone publicly
cards.example: I showed solidarity instead of quietly agreeing later.

cards.definition: the feeling of being the same kind of person
cards.example: There was instant kinship, we both build things alone.

cards.definition: loyalty you have chosen and stated
cards.example: My allegiance is to the plan, not the mood.

cards.definition: staying with someone when it costs you
cards.example: Loyalty is proven in the inconvenient moment.

cards.definition: the belief that someone will do what they said
cards.example: Trust is built by small kept promises, not big ones.

cards.definition: open honesty, even when it is awkward
cards.example: Candor early prevents a fight later.

cards.definition: letting someone see a real weak spot
cards.example: Vulnerability is strength when it is chosen, not leaked.

cards.definition: being fully there with the person in front of you
cards.example: Presence beats every clever line.

cards.definition: noticing and responding to what they need
cards.example: Be attentive without hovering.

cards.definition: open to what someone is offering
cards.example: She was receptive because I asked instead of told.

cards.definition: easy for people to come talk to
cards.example: Approachable is a posture, not a personality.

cards.definition: holds attention in a good way
cards.example: He is engaging because he asks better questions.

cards.definition: takes the defensiveness out of someone
cards.example: A disarming admission ended the whole argument.

cards.definition: people move toward you without knowing why
cards.example: Magnetic is what I used to be at a table of strangers.

cards.definition: real, not put on
cards.example: People can tell genuine from performed in about four seconds.

cards.definition: thinks about the effect on other people
cards.example: Considerate is small and constant, not grand.

cards.definition: puts real thought into what someone needs
cards.example: A thoughtful question beats an expensive gift.

cards.definition: backs someone up in a way they can feel
cards.example: Supportive means showing up, not agreeing with everything.

cards.definition: gives someone the push to keep going
cards.example: Be encouraging about effort, specific about results.

cards.definition: showing you value what someone did
cards.example: Appreciative and specific, always both.

cards.definition: openly noticing what someone did or said
cards.example: Acknowledgment is the cheapest thing that lands the hardest.

cards.definition: confirming someone's feeling is reasonable
cards.example: Validation is not agreement, it is recognition.

cards.definition: stating out loud that someone is what they are
cards.example: Give people a reputation to live up to.

cards.definition: the sense of being part of each other's life
cards.example: Connection comes from asking, not from giving.
